about: The inputs of tools/review/measure_screen.py for three films of the same script. The tool takes flags and reads one folder per film under --dir, not this file: write each file below into every film's folder, then run the command from the repository root. Values are illustrative. <review> is the comparison folder, <project>/review/YYYY-MM-DD-slug; 61 is the word count of kit/templates/script/manifest.example.json.

flags.--dir: the comparison folder, with one subfolder per film
flags.--films: optional: the film folders to measure, comma-separated (default: every subfolder with shots.json)
flags.--reference-words: the fixed script's word count; each film's words a minute is this over its speech span
flags.--first-word: optional: report when a heard word containing this is first spoken
flags.--out: the result (default <dir>/measures.json): per film the verdict counts and shares of runtime, text items and edge density per frame, speech span and words a minute

per_film_folder.frames/: one frame per shot, at its midpoint, named as in shots.json

notes: A shot gives a frame (a path in the film's folder, whose edge density the tool measures with ffmpeg) or a precomputed edge_density_pct, and either text_items or on_screen_text (items separated by | , or ;). Count the names and labels on screen, not captions.

Verdicts are carries, partly or competes, from the per-shot test (uvk-film-audit), judged the same way for every film. A shot may carry its own verdict instead of verdicts.json, but then every shot must.
Mark shot boundaries by hand where a film crossfades: scene detection at a threshold of 0.25 found only 8 of one film's 35 transitions here (research/METHODS.md).
Drop the words heard after the last script word before measuring pace: Whisper loops phrases over music and silence.
